subject: general
question: The Bada Imambara is located on the banks of which river?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Gomti**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Bada Imambara**, also known as the **Asafi Imambara**, is an iconic historical monument situated in **Lucknow**, the capital of **Uttar Pradesh**.
 
• It is located on the southern bank of the **Gomti River**, which is a major tributary of the **Ganges** and flows through the heart of the city.
 
• The structure was built by **Nawab Asaf-ud-Daula** in **1784** as part of a **famine relief project** to provide livelihoods to the people of the **Awadh** region during a severe drought.
 
• Architecturally, the monument is renowned for its **central vaulted hall**, which is approximately 15 meters high and was constructed without the use of **beams** or **pillars**, representing a feat of 18th-century engineering.
 
• The complex includes the **Asafi Mosque**, the **Shahi Baoli** (step-well), and the famous **Bhulbhulaiya**, a complex **labyrinth** of interconnected passages located above the main hall.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gomti River**:

 
 
• It originates from **Gomat Taal** (Fulhaar Jheel) near **Pilibhit**, Uttar Pradesh.
 
• The river flows through several important cities including **Lakhimpur Kheri**, **Lucknow**, **Sultanpur**, and **Jaunpur** before joining the **Ganga**.
 
 
 
• **Ganga**:
 
 
• The longest river in India, it originates from the **Gangotri Glacier** in the **Uttarakhand** Himalayas.
 
 
 
• **Yamuna**:
 
 
• Originates from the **Yamunotri Glacier** and flows through major cities like **Delhi** and **Agra** before merging with the Ganga at **Prayagraj**.
 
 
 
• **Kaveri**:
 
 
• A major river in **Southern India** that originates from the **Brahmagiri Hills** in the **Western Ghats** of **Karnataka** and flows through **Tamil Nadu**.
